en.title: Vermilion
en.p1: I first encountered qi lacquer not in China, but through its absence from it.
en.p2: Living abroad, I began noticing how deeply the craft had taken root in Japan — in the care given to urushi vessels, in the way the material was taught, preserved, celebrated. It was only then that I learned: lacquer originated in China, over 8,000 years ago. Something that had always been part of my cultural inheritance had become easier to see from a distance.
en.p3: At its core, qi (漆, qī) — the raw resin harvested from the lacquer tree — is built up in layers, sometimes dozens, each coat slowly cured, polished, then buried under the next. The result is a surface that feels less like a coating and more like accumulated time — depth you sense, not just see. Its palette, at its most essential, is two colours: vermilion and black. Red from cinnabar, black from iron. Ancient, material, irreducible.
en.p4: Returning to China — to Jingdezhen — felt like coming home and starting over at the same time. Through experimentation, I found a rare glaze that, once fired, carries something of qi's depth and surface quality. The series explores the gradient between these two colours — vermilion burning slowly into black — not through the patient accumulation of lacquer layers, but through the kiln itself: glaze and fire negotiating the transition in a single firing.
en.p5: Qi lacquer is a recognised Chinese Intangible Cultural Heritage, a tradition at risk of disappearing. This series does not attempt to replicate it, but to carry something of its spirit into a different material — a conversation across craft traditions rather than a copy of one.
en.closing: 遗朱 — the vermilion that remains — is about what survives the distance, and what we only learn to value once we've had to look for it.

zh.title: 《遗朱》
zh.p1: 我第一次真正注意到大漆，并不是在中国，而是因为在中国几乎已经很少见到它。
zh.p2: 在海外生活时，我开始慢慢意识到，这门工艺在日本是如何深深扎根的——人们对漆器的珍视，对材料与工艺的细致对待，以及它在教育、传承与日常生活中的存在。也是在那个时候，我才重新认识到：大漆其实起源于中国，已有八千多年的历史。某种本来属于自己文化传统的一部分，反而是在离开之后，才被看得更加清楚。
zh.p3: 从本质上说，大漆是从漆树中采集的天然树脂。它的形成依赖于层层叠加：有时需要涂覆几十层，每一层都要经过缓慢的固化与打磨，再被下一层覆盖。最终呈现出的表面，与其说是一层涂层，不如说更像是时间不断沉积的结果——一种不仅能够被看到，也能够被感受到的深度。它最基本的色彩只有两种：朱红与黑。红来自辰砂，黑来自铁。古老而纯粹，带着强烈的物质感。
zh.p4: 后来，当我回到中国，来到景德镇时，那种感觉既像回家，又像重新开始。在不断的实验中，我找到了一种釉料，在高温烧成后能够呈现出某种接近漆的深度与表面质感。这组作品尝试探索的，是朱红与黑之间的渐变关系——朱红在黑色中缓慢地沉入、过渡。但这种变化并不是通过一层层漆的耐心堆叠来完成，而是交由窑火：在一次烧成中，让釉与火共同作用，生成这种颜色之间的过渡。
zh.p5: 大漆工艺是中国的国家级非物质文化遗产，但同时也正面临逐渐式微的处境。这组作品并不是对漆工艺的复制，而是尝试将它的某种精神带入另一种材料之中。与其说是模仿，不如说是一种跨越工艺之间的对话。
zh.closing: "遗朱"——留下的一抹朱红，也暗合"遗珠"。那些被时间与距离遮蔽的传统，如同遗落的明珠，在重新被找寻之时，熠熠生辉。

en.about.p1: Tianan Zhang is a material-based artist working between film photography, ceramics, and moving image. Her practice explores surface, tactility, and the quiet transformations produced through light, glaze, and time.
en.about.p2: Moving between image-making and object-making, her work often treats ceramic surfaces as visual fields where color, texture, and atmosphere interact. Across photography and clay, she is interested in how materials record gesture, memory, and subtle shifts of perception.
